meta.title: Illustrative packaging factors
meta.status: ILLUSTRATIVE — prototype screening values, not certified LCA data
meta.note: Cradle-to-gate production of 1 kg of packaging material. 'mass_ratio' on an alternative is the assumed mass of the replacement needed per kg of the original, because lighter materials are not always a like-for-like swap.

units.typical_recyclability: fraction typically captured for recycling where collection exists

alternative.cost: Board is usually cheaper per kg but more mass is needed; net cost is often similar.
alternative.feasibility_note: Works for dry goods and multipacks; needs a change of packing line.
trade_offs: Roughly twice the packaging mass is assumed, which raises transport weight.
No moisture barrier — unsuitable where products must stay dry in transit.
If the board is landfilled rather than recycled it can emit methane as it degrades.

alternative.cost: Tooling for moulded pulp is an up-front cost; unit cost is comparable at volume.
alternative.feasibility_note: Needs custom tooling and drop-testing for fragile products.
trade_offs: Heavier for the same cushioning, raising transport weight.
Less protection against moisture and repeated impact.

options.name: Corrugated cardboard (virgin fibre)
options.basis: Illustrative; corrugated board, mostly virgin fibre.

alternative.feasibility_note: Standard product from most box suppliers.
trade_offs: Slightly lower stacking strength, so a marginally heavier board grade is assumed.

options.name: Recycled cardboard
options.basis: Illustrative; high recycled-fibre board, cut-off approach.

options.name: Recycled plastic film
options.basis: Illustrative; film with high post-consumer recycled content.
